text:
Alice M: FYI customer acme-corp is seeing a spike of 504s when starting streaming longpolls to hosted API since ~09:30 UTC. ~30% of start requests failing, steady since deploy. Sample trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d.

Alice M: curl repro (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant: acme" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=rw-13b \
  --data-binary @payload.json
```

Alice M: Envoy at edge returns 504, upstream logs show RST/RESET around stream start. Quick snippet from edge logs: `2026-03-16T09:31:02Z edge-1 svc=envoy caller=router.cpp:123 upstream_reset: stream reset: RST_STREAM`

Ben P: Do we have per-tenant upstream pool metrics? which midproxy is being used for acme? any GOAWAY or h2 window messages?

Alice M: Tenant routed to midproxy pool mid-eu-3, route id /v1/stream (stream-start). I pulled a few traces: trace-0a1b2c3d, trace-0f9e8d7c. No obvious 5xx from model hosts — looks like connection never establishes, upstream times out after 30s.

Carol S: My gut: keepalive/connpool exhaustion or h2 stream window drift at midproxy. Also possible ejection from midproxy due to ephemeral health check flapping. Steps to triage:
- check `envoy.cluster.upstream_cx_active` and `upstream_rq_pending_overflow` for mid-eu-3
- look for GOAWAY/connection_error in envoy logs
- correlate with tenant auth-fanout (auth cache slow responses can stall streams)

Ben P: Can you paste the minimal headers/body that reproduces? also attach a short `tcpdump` if we need to confirm RST vs timeout.

Alice M: Repro payload attached to ticket. Quick header sample: `X-Tenant: acme`, `Accept: text/event-stream`, `Timeout: 60`. I'll try capture next 15m.

Monitoring Bot: Alert: support.edge.504_rate spike (tenant=acme) 09:30-09:45 UTC — 504 rate 28% (baseline 0.4%).

Carol S: For immediate mitigation: rotate tenant to reserve pool (mid-eu-standby) OR bump envoy upstream timeout to 60s for that route so streams don't get prematurely timed out during handshake. Also temporarily disable tenant-level rate-limiter if auth is slow.

Ben P: I can do a quick scale on mid-eu-3 (+2 replicas) and open a canary route to mid-eu-standby. Which option do you want?

Alice M: Let's do both: scale +2 and route acme to standby pool for 30m while we collect tcpdump/traces. I'll apply upstream_timeout=60s for /v1/stream canary.

Ben P: Scaling now. Applying route patch to standby pool and timeout tweak.

Monitoring Bot: Notice: route patch applied by Ben P @ 09:47 UTC.

Alice M: Quick update: after moving to standby and bumping timeout, 504s dropped to ~1.4% in the last 10m. Collecting tcpdump for traces.

Carol S: Good. Next steps:
- collect full envoy logs + upstream host logs for the timeframe
- check midproxy healthchecks and circuit ejection logs for mid-eu-3 (were any hosts ejected around 09:28-09:35?)
- run a controlled repro with lower concurrency to isolate if connpool saturates

Alice M: Agree. I'm opening a support ticket and will attach tcpdump + envoys + trace ids. We'll schedule a postmortem if root cause isn't auth-cache related.

Ben P: Thx — ping me in the ticket if you need a retrospective. :thumbsup:

Carol S: Also add a quick note in the change log that we temporarily increased upstream_timeout for that route and rotated tenant — revert after postmortem.

Alice M: Will do. Thanks everyone.

Ben P: Closing triage here for now; reopen if 504s resurge.

Alice M: Closing — customer notified and workaround applied. :white_check_mark:
